caption: Jesus offers living water at the Feast of Tabernacles. The festival setting matters—but Leviticus’s drink offering was a different ritual, poured out to God.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did a drink offering predict Jesus? Leviticus lists drink offerings at a festival. During that festival, Jesus invites thirsty people to come to him and drink.
slides.body: Leviticus lists drink offerings at a festival. During that festival, Jesus invites thirsty people to come to him and drink.
slides.heading: Did a drink offering predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Lev 23:36-37: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its designated day.
slides.body: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its designated day.

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 7:37–39, BSB: ‘If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.’ He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive.
slides.body: ‘If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.’ He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 7:37–39

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why the setting matters The festival later included a water-pouring ceremony. Jesus uses that powerful setting to present himself as the source of living water and God’s Spirit.
slides.body: The festival later included a water-pouring ceremony. Jesus uses that powerful setting to present himself as the source of living water and God’s Spirit.
slides.heading: Why the setting matters

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But these are different drinks Leviticus’s drink offering was poured out to God. Jesus offers living water to people. The festival link is real, but this ritual is not a prediction.
